body.statement: Does \(q(v)>0\) for every \(v\in\Omega_V\), together with the calibrated restrictions \(\rho\ge\delta\) and \(d_M\ge\delta\), imply both that every moment vector of an arbitrary admissible SCM has an equal-moment representative in the bounded finite legal fiber and that every limiting vector of bounded graph-legal moments has an equal-moment finite SCM whose actual selected MAG remains in \(\mathcal G(\mathcal P)\)? Resolve first the binary three-observed-variable COPAG with a compelled collider by stratifying the invariant essential-feature polynomials \(Z_e\). An affirmative resolution must give a legal lift for every boundary stratum; a negative resolution must give a positive rational \(q\), a rational \(\delta\), and an algebraic endpoint for which the negative certificate \(\mathsf{Cert}(t)\) excludes every legal architecture.
body.justification: This remains the sole nonroutine topological bottleneck between exact actual-parent graph semantics and attained extrema for the full arbitrary-SCM fiber.
body.gap: The isolated-selection compelled-collider subcase has a legal lift, but neither faithfulness-density results nor saturated finite architecture enumeration settles selected graphs with latent or selection ancestry.
body.consumer: Its resolution determines whether arbitrary-SCM selection-COPAG bounds may be reported as attained; until then, only bounded-image certificates and subclass attainment have that interpretation.

obligation.what_is_open: For a positive but potentially unfaithful selected law \(q\), prove or refute that every arbitrary admissible moment vector and every limit of bounded exact-graph moment vectors has an equal-moment representative in the bounded fiber with actual selected MAG in \(\mathcal G(\mathcal P)\).
obligation.obstruction: The selected-cell and intervention moments are separately linear in each source law, whereas \(Z_{\operatorname{src}(C,j)}\) is quadratic in its own source law.  Even inside a saturated super-architecture, exact barycentric preservation can delete the last positive witness on a proper face, and the frozen assumptions impose neither faithfulness nor a minimum essentiality margin.  Exogenizing hidden endogenous structure must also preserve actual functional parents rather than only a permitted latent projection.
obligation.attempted: Saturating every order removes combinatorial architecture maximality but not the nonlinear witness obstruction.  Adding directed-feature indicators to the barycentric vector preserves those separately linear features, but not the two-copy source-feature polynomials.  Prescribing positive witness atoms is incompatible with an arbitrary boundary barycenter.  The positive exclusive-or support-deletion family demonstrates failure of naive compression, although an equal-moment legal lift repairs that example.  The compelled-collider test closes only for the isolated-selection-root subcase recorded below.
obligation.partial_result:
The mandatory collider test closes for the following nontrivial subcase.  Let \(V=\{X,Y,Z\}\) be binary, let the retained structural graph be \(X\to Z\leftarrow Y\) with \(S\) an independent selection root, take \(B=\{X\}\), and assume the positive selected law \(q\) obeys the collider Markov restriction \(X\mathbin{\perp\!\!\!\perp}Y\).  Put
\[
 p_{xy}=q(Z=1\mid X=x,Y=y)\in(0,1).
\]
Choose independent \(U_X,U_Y\) with laws \(q_X,q_Y\), an independent \(U_Z\sim\operatorname{Unif}[0,1]\), and measurable sets \(E_{xy}\subset[0,1]\) with Lebesgue measure \(p_{xy}\).  The four sets can be chosen so that \(E_{0y}\ne E_{1y}\) modulo null sets for at least one \(y\), and \(E_{x0}\ne E_{x1}\) modulo null sets for at least one \(x\): begin with intervals of the prescribed lengths, and whenever an equality remains, exchange two sufficiently short subintervals between the set and its complement.  Positivity \(0<p_{xy}<1\) makes each exchange possible, and finitely many disjoint exchanges preserve distinctions already installed.  Define
\[
 X=U_X,\qquad Y=U_Y,\qquad Z=\mathbf 1\{U_Z\in E_{XY}\}.
\]
Then
\[
 \Pr(X=x,Y=y,Z=z)=q_X(x)q_Y(y)q(z\mid x,y)=q(x,y,z),
\]
and the two strict symmetric differences make both arrows into \(Z\) actual functional dependencies, even when \(q\) is unfaithful to one or both arrows.  Taking an independent \(S\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(\rho)\), with \(\rho\in[\delta,1]\), gives \(c_v=\rho q(v)\) and \(d=\rho\).  For every bounded binary outcome map \(h\), truncated factorization gives the single attainable selected-intervention value
\[
 \theta=
 \sum_{y\in\{0,1\}}q_Y(y)
 \bigl[h(0)(1-p_{by})+h(1)p_{by}\bigr].
\]
It is attained by the exact collider construction above.  Thus the exact-graph fiber and all its support-stratum closure points lift in this isolated-selection compelled-collider case.  This does not cover selected MAGs in which \(S\) has parents or latent ancestors, nor does it preserve an arbitrary pair \((n,d)\) beyond the value fixed by this collider factorization.
